raw_case_text:
Male patient, Caucasian, 31 years old, from Sao Martinho da Serra, RS, Brazil. He resides with his wife and his mother. He had a past medical history of testicular tumor at age 24 and was cured after treatment. He had been asymptomatic for five years. 
On 07/01/2012, he started having fever (40.2 C). He sought medical treatment with the assistant oncologist, who requested additional tests to rule out tumor recurrence. A total abdominal ultrasonography showed hepatosplenomegaly and retroperitoneal lymph node enlargement. A transthoracic echocardiogram showed signs suggestive of acute pericarditis with an asymptomatic patient from the cardiologic point of view.
On the 15th day of symptoms, due to clinical and body temperature worsening, he sought the emergency care department of a local hospital, where he was treated by an infectologist. At this point, a detailed clinical history was obtained. He had sustained high fever, above 39 C, which did not improve with antipyretics used for the last five days (dipyrone 4 g/day and acetaminophen 3 g/day), accompanied by fetid and profuse night sweats (approximately four changes of clothing a night); asthenia; myalgia, especially in the dorsal region; mood alterations. The patient was a veterinarian who had been exposed to the premature delivery of bovines in the past six months. He denied intake of dairy products at home.
Considering the symptoms and the epidemiology of exposure to cattle, the hypothesis of a brucellosis diagnosis was raised. Laboratory assessment was carried out immediately. The patient was released to undergo home observation and to be reevaluated within 48 hours. In this assessment, the serology screening test (Rose Bengal test) for Brucella sp. IgM was positive, while the IgG fraction was negative. The patient had three blood cultures in progress. Empirical antimicrobial therapy was initiated for brucellosis with doxycycline (dose = 200 mg day) and rifampicin (dose = 900 mg/day).
He was maintained on outpatient assessment and reassessed on 07/22/12, when blood culture results were released, showing to be positive for Gram-negative bacilli. New serologic tests for brucellosis were requested. The IgM fraction remained positive, while there was seroconversion from negative to positive IgG antibody to brucellosis. Treatment was maintained with the above-mentioned doses.
Other general laboratory tests showed slight increase in transaminases and positive antinuclear antibodies (speckled pattern). For other test results, see Table 1.
The patient was asymptomatic after 10 days of treatment. On reassessment after 30 days, he showed improved overall health status with the presence of mild night sweats, increased appetite and return to work activities. He had been afebrile for more than three weeks. Treatment was maintained at the above-mentioned doses and was completed in 42 days.
After 60 days of symptom onset, the patient was asymptomatic and afebrile. He was discharged and received instructions in case of symptom recurrence.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old male presented with a 15-day history of sustained high fever (>39 °C, reaching 40.2 °C) refractory to antipyretics, profuse fetid night sweats, asthenia, and dorsal myalgia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed high fever up to 40.2 °C on 07/01/2012. He initially consulted his oncologist to rule out tumor recurrence, undergoing ultrasonography and echocardiography. Over the subsequent 2 weeks, fever and symptoms worsened despite 5 days of antipyretics (dipyrone 4 g/day and acetaminophen 3 g/day). On illness day 15, he presented to the emergency department with sustained high fever (>39 °C), fetid night sweats requiring approximately 4 clothing changes per night, asthenia, dorsal myalgia, and mood changes, prompting infectious disease evaluation and diagnostic workup.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of testicular tumor at age 24, cured following treatment, asymptomatic for 5 years. Occupation: veterinarian, exposed to the premature delivery of bovines within the preceding 6 months. Denied consumption of unpasteurized dairy products at home. Resides in Sao Martinho da Serra, RS, Brazil.
subjective.review_of_systems: Profuse fetid night sweats (~4 clothing changes/night), asthenia, dorsal myalgia, mood alterations. Home medications: dipyrone (4 g/day) and acetaminophen (3 g/day). Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: sustained fever above 39 °C, reaching 40.2 °C. General: asthenic, mood alterations. Cardiologic examination normal. Other systemic physical examination findings not documented.
objective.routine_investigations: Total abdominal ultrasonography: hepatosplenomegaly and retroperitoneal lymph node enlargement. General laboratory tests: slight increase in transaminases; antinuclear antibodies (ANA) positive (speckled pattern). Blood cultures: 3 blood cultures collected on day 15, yielding Gram-negative bacilli on 07/22/2012.
objective.advanced_workup: Transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE): signs suggestive of acute pericarditis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute brucellosis complicated by acute pericarditis and hepatosplenomegaly.
Confirmation: Rose Bengal screening test positive for Brucella sp. IgM (IgG initially negative); repeat serology demonstrated seroconversion to positive IgG antibody for brucellosis with persistent IgM; blood cultures grew Gram-negative bacilli.
Differentials ruled out: Testicular tumor recurrence ruled out by oncologic and ultrasound evaluation.
Treatment & Outcome: Treated with oral doxycycline (200 mg/day) and oral rifampicin (900 mg/day) for 42 days. Patient became asymptomatic after 10 days of treatment, remained afebrile for >3 weeks, exhibited improved general condition and appetite by 30 days, and was afebrile and completely asymptomatic at 60-day follow-up.
